luke.18.p1.b1.text: Then Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray at all times and not lose heart:

luke.18.p1.b2.text: “In a certain town there was a judge who neither feared God nor respected men.

luke.18.p2.b1.text: ‘Though I neither fear God nor respect men, yet because this widow keeps pestering me, I will give her justice. Then she will stop wearing me out with her perpetual requests.’

luke.18.p2.b2.text: Will not God bring about justice for His elect who cry out to Him day and night? Will He continue to defer their help?

luke.18.p2.b3.text: Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on earth?”

luke.18.p3.b1.text: To some who trusted in their own righteousness and viewed others with contempt, He also told this parable:

luke.18.p3.b2.text: “Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.

luke.18.p3.b3.text: ‘God, I thank You that I am not like the other men—swindlers, evildoers, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.

luke.18.p4.b1.text: I fast twice a week and pay tithes of all that I acquire.’

luke.18.p4.b2.text: But the tax collector stood at a distance, unwilling even to lift up his eyes to heaven. Instead, he beat his breast and said,

luke.18.p4.b3.text: ‘God, have mercy on me, a sinner!’

luke.18.p4.b4.text: I tell you, this man, rather than the Pharisee, went home justified.

luke.18.p5.b1.text: Now people were even bringing their babies to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them. And when the disciples saw this, they rebuked those who brought them.

luke.18.p5.b2.text: “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

luke.18.p5.b3.text: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”

luke.18.p6.b1.text: “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”

luke.18.p6.b2.text: “Why do you call Me good?” … “No one is good except God alone.

luke.18.p6.b3.text: ‘Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and mother.’

luke.18.p6.b4.text: “All these I have kept from my youth,”

luke.18.p7.b2.text: Sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”

luke.18.p7.b3.text: But when the ruler heard this, he became very sad, because he was extremely wealthy.

luke.18.p8.b1.text: “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!

luke.18.p8.b2.text: Indeed, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”

luke.18.p8.b4.text: “What is impossible with man is possible with God.”

luke.18.p9.b1.text: “Look,” … “we have left all we had to follow You.”

luke.18.p9.b2.text: “Truly I tell you,” … “no one who has left home or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God

luke.18.p9.b3.text: will fail to receive many times more in this age—and in the age to come, eternal life.”

luke.18.p10.b1.text: Then Jesus took the Twelve aside and said to them,

luke.18.p10.b2.text: “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything the prophets have written about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.

luke.18.p10.b3.text: He will be delivered over to the Gentiles … and on the third day He will rise again.”

luke.18.p10.b4.text: But the disciples did not understand any of these things. The meaning was hidden from them, and they did not comprehend what He was saying.

luke.18.p11.b1.text: As Jesus drew near to Jericho, a blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.

luke.18.p11.b2.text: When he heard the crowd going by, he asked what was happening.

luke.18.p12.b1.text: “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”

luke.18.p12.b2.text: Those who led the way admonished him to be silent,

luke.18.p12.b3.text: “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

luke.18.p13.b1.text: Jesus stopped and directed that the man be brought to Him. When he had been brought near, Jesus asked him,

luke.18.p13.b2.text: “What do you want Me to do for you?”

luke.18.p14.b1.text: “Receive your sight!” … “Your faith has healed you.”

luke.18.p15.b2.text: And all the people who saw this gave praise to God.
